gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Nippo's small letters stand up almost as tall as its capitals, each stroke looking cut from bent wire. Noto Sans Warang Citi counters with words that sit as solid blocks.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-yi: Wiry, technical, and oddly tall. Noto Sans Yi has a deep midsection and rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook, so a long stretch of it reads open and unhurried.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-squa: Nippo's lowercase stands nearly as tall as its capitals, with strokes that look cut from wire. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square then soars with its own tall x-height and wide gaps, and the two feel like cousins who happen to dress differently.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-traditional-nushu: Noto Traditional Nushu reads like a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls shut, with bowls filling the line. And over a longer passage, Nippo's wire-cut headings keep it feeling approachable rather than stiff.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-numans: Nippo's small letters stand almost capital-tall. Its curves match the stems exactly, which sits sharply against Numans, whose widely tracked lowercase and far-hanging s feel loose and airy.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-onest: Onest reads gently, with short ascenders over big bowls and lines of uniform thickness. Onest's softness is the strongest quality here, set against Nippo's wire-cut, nearly capital-sized lowercase up top.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-open-sans: Nippo's strokes look like a bent paperclip, with lowercase standing almost capital-tall. Open Sans follows with bulky lowercase proportions and a smooth read, so the heading feels sharp while the text stays easy on the page.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-orienta: Nippo leads with proud, almost capital-sized small letters, each stroke looking cut from wire and never swelling like a brush. Orienta's breathing counters and near-uniform case heights give the pair its quiet strength.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-oxygen: Nippo outlines its letters with one steady thickness, and its small letters nearly reach capital height. And Oxygen takes over where that wiry display type stops, with curves that stay open and a lowercase close to the capitals.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-parkinsans: Wire-cut, technical, and tall in the lowercase. Parkinsans matches that with one stroke thickness everywhere and wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp shrunk down, so Nippo's edge never feels alone.
